findings.mechanism: When the inspector first computes a score before an accepted evidence item expires, subsequent inspector reads in the same UTC hour reuse that score as long as workspace revision is unchanged. Expiry changes no revision. The cached status and evidence coverage therefore remain verified/covered until the next hour, although the current evidence is invalid and the framework view has recomputed at-risk. This can mislead an approver inspecting a requirement for up to nearly one hour.
findings.evidence: Runtime reproduction at pinned HEAD: integrity-fixture.mjs creates an implemented, verified CSF requirement and bound accepted evidence expiring at 12:30, reads nodeDetail at 12:10, then reads again at 12:40 without any mutation. integrity-fixture.log records evidenceCurrentlyValid=false, inspectorStatus=verified, inspectorEvidenceCoverage=1, frameworkStatus=at-risk, frameworkValidEvidenceCount=0. Counterevidence: frameworkState (views.ts:148) and workspaceSummary deliberately recompute with current metadata; their corrected behavior does not cover nodeDetail. Evidence validity itself correctly rejects the expired item; the defect is the remaining hour cache consumer.
findings.recommendation: Compute nodeDetail score from the same fresh metadata and clock used for its returned evidence/state, as frameworkState already does; alternatively expire cached scores at the earliest evidence/review/task transition instead of only the hour boundary. Add a targeted regression that reads the inspector before and after a within-hour expiry without a revision change.

limitations: This bounded review is not exhaustive proof of correctness. Full pnpm check and dependency audit are owned by the lead and were not run here.

PostgreSQL locking, transactions and migrations were reviewed in source only; no PostgreSQL instance or multi-process migration race was exercised by this node. S3 adapter was reviewed in source only; no external object service or credentials were accessed.

No live tenant, container, deployed service, production backup or actual recovery target was read or mutated. Recovery evidence uses only a small synthetic SQLite/local-blob fixture; it does not establish hosted recovery, capacity, key recovery, retention or power-loss durability.

Backup consistency depends on the documented operator assertion that all writers and parent-directory mutations are stopped. Included backup hashes are not authenticity; separately protected manifest/checkpoint retention and restore-time authentication configuration remain operator responsibilities.
Identity repository entry points were surveyed for storage context; authentication policy and authorization coverage belong to the separate security lens. No browser rendering was exercised here.
